attributes.tc_description: A tiger hides by remaining still against a similar-looking background and behind sparse vegetation. Some body area remains exposed along a usable thermal line of sight, but characteristic RGB features and lidar geometry are insufficient for reliable classification. Fully opaque concealment and inadequate thermal contrast remain outside the claimed benefit of adding LWIR.
A visually or thermally cluttered background makes the target hard to separate from surrounding structure.
Low ambient light reduces useful visible-spectrum information and shifts the intended sensing contribution to other modalities.
Rain attenuation and clutter reduce sensing information without a hardware or software fault.
The target thermal signature approaches the background signature, including thermal crossover conditions.
The target is partially hidden by other objects or terrain, so only incomplete features are available.
Environmental material or vegetation obstructs the sensing aperture while the sensor otherwise functions correctly.
The target occupies few spatial samples because of range, viewpoint, or projected size.
Bright incident illumination reduces useful visible-image information without a sensor defect.
A tiger assumes a pose or articulation poorly represented by the classifier, while the sensing and execution chain remains fault-free.
